item.title: Article: Governed Autonomous Intelligence for Mission-Critical Utility (Source: feed.infoq.com)
item.description:
The article describes an architecture for agentic AI in regulated utility operations. Agents reason and propose actions, but a deterministic policy gate and a governed tool gateway control execution, with human approval where required. It covers an AWS reference implementation, grounding in runbooks, governed prediction, outcome validation, audit evidence, and phased autonomy.

By Purnang Borah

item.title: Presentation: AI-Assisted Software Delivery: from Code to Production (Source: feed.infoq.com)
item.description:
The panelists explore how engineering teams adapt delivery architectures, pipelines, security, and governance for AI-assisted development. They share practical strategies for verifying AI-generated code, solving testing and deployment bottlenecks, maintaining human oversight, and measuring AI's true impact on software velocity, quality, reliability, and operational cost.

By Garima Bajpaj, Martin Reynolds, Patrick Debois, Gunnar Grosch, Renato Losio

item.title: Presentation: Modernising Retail at Scale: Architecting a Cloud-to-Edge Platform for a Global Enterprise (Source: feed.infoq.com)
item.description:
Jayesh Bhayani discusses Tesco's decade-long enterprise transformation from fragmented legacy systems to a unified cloud-edge platform. He explains how aligning system, talent, and process modernizations allowed Tesco to scale mission-critical retail operations to millions of customers, while sharing practical lessons on build vs. buy, cloud cost management, and preparing for agentic commerce.

By Jayesh Bhayani

item.title: Presentation: Inferencing for Enterprises (Source: feed.infoq.com)
item.description:
Dio Rettori discusses the operational realities of enterprise AI inference. Moving beyond fast token generation, he explores why inference requires dedicated systems engineering, tackles GPU utilization pitfalls, compares on-prem versus cloud TCO, and analyzes multi-agent latency determinism. He shares why teams must embed domain ontology directly into models rather than relying solely on RAG.

By Dio Rettori
